title: One catch-all route, any Fitting id, to a rendered view
summary: `/fitting/drill` is served by a single dynamic catch-all page that mounts one client panel. That panel reads the `fittingId` and `rest` params off the URL, guards them against the live library and composition, then hands the sub-path to a tiny route matcher that maps the id's declared views to one `UiView`; the matched view renders through `FittingView`. The same machinery resolves any Fitting id — `drill` itself declares no `ui.views`, so it falls through the matcher to its own-port status branch.

states.label: Drill view
states.description: The drillbook asks that the embedded Drill surface load as a usable product view — clear navigation and status, no raw API data, no blank content, no confusing nested chrome. There is no page hand-written for `drill`: `/fitting/<id>` is one dynamic catch-all that resolves ANY Fitting id to a rendered view, and this flow follows that resolution end to end.

steps.title: The route is one catch-all that mounts a single panel
steps.description: `/fitting/drill` — and every `/fitting/<id>[/<rest>]` — resolves to this one dynamic segment page. It loads no data and hardcodes no Fitting: it just returns `FittingSurfacePanel`, the client component that does all the resolution. There is nothing `drill`-specific on disk; the id is a URL parameter, read next.

steps.title: The panel reads the id and rest straight off the URL
steps.description: `FittingSurfacePanel` pulls `fittingId` (`drill`) and the `rest` catch-all segments out of Next's route params, joining `rest` back into a leading-slash sub-path (`/` when there is no deep link). Everything else it needs — the composition and the library — comes from the app shell, not a fetch. These two values are the entire input to the resolver.

steps.title: The id must be a known, stationed Fitting
steps.description: Before any view is resolved the id is validated twice: it must exist in the Armory `library` AND be selected in the current composition. This is the guard against stale links to retired Fittings — a bad id gets a plain "not found" / "not stationed" message, never a blank pane or raw data. Only a Fitting that clears both gates reaches the matcher.

steps.title: The sub-path is matched against the Fitting's declared views
steps.description: This is the id-to-view step. `matchView` walks the Fitting's `ui.views[]` (filtered to `sidebar-surface` placement) and returns the first whose `route` template aligns with the sub-path, capturing any `:param` segments — a deliberately tiny react-router-style matcher, no regex or catch-alls. The banded line is the resolution: a `UiView` plus its params, or `null` when nothing lines up.

steps.title: A matched view renders through FittingView; drill has none
steps.description: When `matchView` returns a match, the panel mounts `FittingView` with the resolved view and captured params — this is the faculty-tab / embedded-view path that turns a `UiView` into a real component. The honest wrinkle for `drill`: its manifest declares no `ui.views`, so `match` is null and there is no deep link, dropping it to the `ownPort` branch (`OwnPortStatusPanel`) — the status/controls strip for a Fitting whose live UI embeds on its own port. Same resolver, different terminal branch.
